task.description: Implement REQ-023 per lib/letflow/design/req023-event-store-schema.md, which passed the Step 1b hard gate unmodified (CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR PASS, handoff 97b4559). Build the six migrations and six Ecto.Schema modules, apply the mandatory prefix() guard pattern from REQ-022's design section 4 to every migration, register all six in tenant_scoped_migrations/0, and fix that function's confirmed module-loading defect (in scope under Unblock-Everything: it blocks this requirement's own acceptance criterion 1). Carry CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's three MINOR findings into the implementation rather than dropping them -- they are listed in the dispatch instructions. Demonstrate acceptance criterion 1 with real, quoted command output against a genuinely provisioned non-default tenant schema; do not report it as satisfied on the strength of the code reading alone.
acceptance_criteria: priv/repo/migrations gains migrations for events, instance_sequence, event_payload_store, events_archive, the idempotency sidecar table, and instance_projections, all using Ecto's :prefix option and applying cleanly against at least one provisioned tenant schema via REQ-022's migration-replay mechanism
events' migration defines the primary key as (event_id, created_at), not a bare event_id, per 0003 Decision C point 2(a)

the events Ecto.Schema module has no update_changeset/2 or any function that issues an UPDATE against a committed row; the moduledoc states this is a deliberate immutability invariant per 0003 Decision C point 1
the idempotency sidecar table has a unique index on idempotency_key and its own moduledoc states it supersedes event_store.md's Open Question #1 two-phase-check recommendation per 0003's resolution
instance_projections' moduledoc explicitly states its schema is event-store scope (this requirement) while its meaningful population is EE-01/S3 scope, not built here
a plain global migrate run creates NONE of the six tables in the public/default schema (the guard pattern's whole purpose), demonstrated by an actual information_schema query

result.summary: Implemented REQ-023 exactly per lib/letflow/design/req023-event-store-schema.md (commit 2f7a8b8), with no behavioural divergence from the design anywhere -- nothing in it turned out to be wrong, so there is no disagreement to route back to CODE-DESIGNER. SIX MIGRATIONS in priv/repo/migrations/, one table per file per 0003 Decision A: 20260816120001_create_events.exs (composite PRIMARY KEY (event_id, created_at) per AC2 and 0003 Decision C 2(a); created_at :utc_datetime_usec defaulting to fragment (now() AT TIME ZONE 'utc') rather than bare now(); payload/metadata :map -> jsonb default %{}; global_seq :bigserial so Postgres puts the owning sequence inside the tenant schema with no raw execute/2 DDL; tenant_id :binary_id with no default; indexes uq_event_sequence (unique, instance_id+sequence_number), idx_events_global_seq, idx_events_instance_time, idx_events_type; deliberately NO uq_event_idempotency, NO idx_events_instance_seq duplicate, NO foreign keys), 20260816120002_create_instance_sequence.exs, 20260816120003_create_instance_projections.exs (partial index idx_proj_status WHERE status = 'ACTIVE'), 20260816120004_create_event_payload_store.exs (composite FK (event_id, event_created_at) -> events(event_id, created_at) ON DELETE RESTRICT, unique uq_event_payload_event on event_id), 20260816120005_create_events_archive.exs, 20260816120006_create_event_idempotency.exs (unique uq_event_idempotency_key on idempotency_key per AC4, plus idx_event_idempotency_event). SIX ECTO.SCHEMA MODULES in lib/letflow/event_store/: event.ex, archived_event.ex, instance_sequence.ex, instance_projection.ex, stored_payload.ex, idempotency_record.ex -- field lists, @primary_key settings, @type t, @spec-ed changesets and the deliberately-absent-function list all exactly as design section 5.1 specifies, with no @schema_prefix on any of the six (INV-EV-8). AC3 verified mechanically: grep over lib/letflow/event_store/*.ex for 'def update_changeset' or 'def changeset' returns exactly one hit, instance_projection.ex:77 -- Event, ArchivedEvent, StoredPayload, IdempotencyRecord and InstanceSequence expose insert_changeset/2 only. Design section 7's required verbatim moduledoc text for AC3, AC4 and AC5 is present byte-for-byte in event.ex, idempotency_record.ex and instance_projection.ex respectively (checked by literal grep on the opening and closing sentences of each block). BOTH MANDATORY HALVES OF REQ-022 DESIGN SECTION 4 ARE PRESENT: (a) every one of the six change/0 bodies is wrapped in 'if prefix() do ... end' with a literal no-op nil branch, matching the shipped reference at test/support/req022_migration_fixture.ex:24-30; (b) all six {version, module} tuples are registered in Letflow.TenantProvisioning.tenant_scoped_migrations/0. IN-SCOPE DEFECT FIX (Unblock-Everything): tenant_scoped_migrations/0's body now loads each migration module before returning its tuple, via a private ensure_migration_module_loaded!/2 that short-circuits on Code.ensure_loaded?/1 and otherwise Code.require_file/1s Path.join([Application.app_dir(:letflow, 'priv'), 'repo', 'migrations', filename]), driven by a new @tenant_scoped_migration_manifest module attribute of {version, module, filename} triples whose third element never escapes the function. Both shipped REQ-022 @specs (tenant_scoped_migrations/0 and replay_migrations/2) are byte-identical; only the body and the stale @doc changed. THE DEFECT IS REAL, NOT THEORETICAL -- demonstrated in a fresh VM (scratch/req023_loading_defect_proof.exs, MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 MIX_ENV=test mix run) against an already-migrated letflow_test2, using a brand-new probe schema so the version was genuinely pending and actually reached Ecto.Migrator.load_migration!/1: 'BEFORE tenant_scoped_migrations/0: Code.ensure_loaded?(CreateEvents) => false', then 'Counterfactual -- Ecto.Migrator.run/4 with a bare {version, module} tuple (REQ-022's shipped shape), module NOT loaded, version PENDING in schema req023_loading_probe_1:' / '  RAISED Ecto.MigrationError: module Letflow.Repo.Migrations.CreateEvents is not an Ecto.Migration'; then in the same VM via the fixed function 'Code.ensure_loaded?(CreateEvents) => true' / '  applied versions = [20260816120001, 20260816120002, 20260816120003, 20260816120004, 20260816120005, 20260816120006]' / '  tables in req023_loading_probe_1: [event_idempotency, event_payload_store, events, events_archive, instance_projections, instance_sequence, schema_migrations]'. COMPILE: MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force -> EXIT=0, output 'Compiling 37 files (.ex)' / 'Generated letflow app'. FORMAT: mix format --check-formatted -> EXIT=0, no output. TESTS: MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test --seed 0 -> EXIT=0, 'Finished in 2.1 seconds (1.0s async, 1.1s sync)' / 'Result: 161 passed (4 properties, 157 tests)' -- exactly the stated 161/161 baseline, no regression. A second run with an unpinned seed also gave EXIT=0 and 'Result: 161 passed (4 properties, 157 tests)'; the known ISS-0011 / GitHub #65 telemetry-attach race at test/letflow/plugs/tenant_status_test.exs:121 did not manifest in either run, and nothing was done to it. ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 1, DEMONSTRATED AGAINST A REAL PROVISIONED TENANT SCHEMA (scratch/req023_ac1_proof.exs, MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 MIX_ENV=test mix run, EXIT=0, database letflow_test2): a real tenant row was inserted via Tenant.create_changeset/3, TenantProvisioning.provision_tenant_schema/1 returned 'provisioned schema_name = tenant_ba535d9c4a0d48878f030c505b9b2af5 (non-default, != public)', tenant_scoped_migrations/0 returned '[{20260816120001, Letflow.Repo.Migrations.CreateEvents}, {20260816120002, Letflow.Repo.Migrations.CreateInstanceSequence}, {20260816120003, Letflow.Repo.Migrations.CreateInstanceProjections}, {20260816120004, Letflow.Repo.Migrations.CreateEventPayloadStore}, {20260816120005, Letflow.Repo.Migrations.CreateEventsArchive}, {20260816120006, Letflow.Repo.Migrations.CreateEventIdempotency}]', and replay_migrations/2 called with its DEFAULT source returned 'replay_migrations/2 (default source) => {:ok, [20260816120001, 20260816120002, 20260816120003, 20260816120004, 20260816120005, 20260816120006]}'. The information_schema query 'SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema = $1 ORDER BY table_name' with $1 = tenant_ba535d9c4a0d48878f030c505b9b2af5 returned, verbatim: '  event_idempotency' '  event_payload_store' '  events' '  events_archive' '  instance_projections' '  instance_sequence' '  schema_migrations' followed by the script's own check 'all six present? true' (schema_migrations is Ecto's per-prefix version-tracking table, expected). Live-catalog cross-checks from the same run: 'events_pkey: PRIMARY KEY (event_id, created_at)' and 'events_archive_pkey: PRIMARY KEY (event_id, created_at)' (AC2); 'event_idempotency / uq_event_idempotency_key: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_event_idempotency_key ON tenant_ba535d9c4a0d48878f030c505b9b2af5.event_idempotency USING btree (idempotency_key)' with no idempotency_key index appearing anywhere on events or events_archive in the full pg_indexes dump (AC4); 'event_payload_store_event_id_fkey: FOREIGN KEY (event_id, event_created_at) REFERENCES tenant_ba535d9c4a0d48878f030c505b9b2af5.events(event_id, created_at) ON DELETE RESTRICT'; 'instance_projections / idx_proj_status: CREATE INDEX idx_proj_status ON ... USING btree (status) WHERE ((status)::text = ''ACTIVE''::text)'; and 'events.global_seq (10) bigint null=NO default=nextval(''tenant_ba535d9c4a0d48878f030c505b9b2af5.events_global_seq_seq''::regclass)', confirming the bigserial sequence landed inside the tenant schema rather than public. The Registration row came back with migrations_applied_at stamped. The probe schema, its tenant_schemas row and its tenants row were all dropped at the end of the run. GUARD-PATTERN NEGATIVE PROOF (AC8): MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.migrate ran all six against the default schema, logging '== Running 20260816120001 Letflow.Repo.Migrations.CreateEvents.change/0 forward' / '== Migrated 20260816120001 in 0.0s' through 20260816120006. The subsequent query 'SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema = ''public'' AND table_name = ANY($1)' with the six names returned 'public tables matching the six REQ-023 names: []' / 'count = 0 (expected 0)', while 'SELECT version FROM public.schema_migrations WHERE version >= 20260816120001 ORDER BY version' returned 'public.schema_migrations rows for the six versions: [20260816120001, 20260816120002, 20260816120003, 20260816120004, 20260816120005, 20260816120006]' -- i.e. all six recorded as applied having created nothing in public, exactly the harmless bookkeeping REQ-022 design section 4 and REQ-023 design section 2.2 predict. The same public query was re-run after the tenant replay and again returned 'count = 0 (expected 0)'. THE THREE MINOR STEP-1b FINDINGS, ALL CARRIED IN, NONE DROPPED. (1) events_archive.created_at carries NO default. Live catalog: 'events_archive.created_at (2) timestamp without time zone null=NO default=nil' against 'events.created_at (2) timestamp without time zone null=NO default=(now() AT TIME ZONE ''utc''::text)'. The migration carries a one-line inline comment at the column plus a numbered paragraph in its header stating why: R-Co gives that column no default on the archive (003_event_archive.sql:15 and 1147_par01_events_partitioning.sql:176 both read created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL with no DEFAULT -- both re-read directly from C:/Users/tvolo/dev/ai-dala/R-Co this step, confirming ORCH's and CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's reading) because the value is copied from the original event, and since created_at is half the composite primary key a defaulted column would let a future REQ-026 archive insert that omitted it silently stamp archive time into the archived event's identity and still commit. (2) event_payload_store.payload is :map -> jsonb, DISCLOSED HERE for REVIEWER's Step 2d consistency check rather than left silent: REQ-023's own description says 'payload (text/bytea)', the design chose jsonb citing R-Co 012_event_retention.sql:19 and 1147:219 (both JSONB) and read-time type-uniformity with events.payload, and no acceptance criterion constrains the choice. Live catalog: 'event_payload_store.payload (4) jsonb null=NO default=nil'. (3) tenant_scoped_migrations/0's shipped @doc is rewritten: it no longer claims the list 'Starts empty', it names REQ-023's six entries and points at @tenant_scoped_migration_manifest, and it documents the new module-loading step in full -- why Ecto.Migrator's load_migration!/1 needs Code.ensure_loaded?/1, why priv/repo/migrations/*.exs is never compiled given mix.exs's elixirc_paths of [lib], why the resulting failure is state-dependent and therefore invisible to REQ-022's own run (only pending migrations reach load_migration!/1, and mix.exs's test: alias runs ecto.migrate in the same VM), and why the Code.ensure_loaded?/1 guard in front of Code.require_file/1 is needed to avoid a redefining-module warning. The @spec is untouched, as the last paragraph of the new @doc states explicitly. SELF-REVIEW (WF-02 Step 2a checklist): no SQL string interpolation of tenant or user input anywhere in the new code -- all six migrations are pure Ecto.Migration DSL with prefix: prefix(), with no execute/1, no execute/2 and no raw SQL at all (INV-7 / design INV-EV-13), and the only pre-existing identifier interpolation in tenant_provisioning.ex (provision_tenant_schema/1's CREATE SCHEMA) was not touched; no bare {:ok, _} = match on any externally-reachable path in the new code (INV-8); no gen_statem, supervisor or transition code touched, so one-supervised-process-per-instance, synchronous transition persistence and README's ASCII state diagram are all unaffected; every new public function carries a @doc and an @spec; the only changed function is tenant_scoped_migrations/0, whose name, arity and @spec are unchanged and whose single call site (replay_migrations/2's default argument) compiles; all six migrations are change/0 using only auto-reversible operations (create table, create index, create unique_index). Scratch verification scripts and logs live in scratch/ (git-ignored); no stray file landed in the project root. handoffs/registry.json was deliberately NOT modified per this step's dispatch instruction that it is ORCH-owned -- flagged below as a MINOR discrepancy against HANDOFF_PROTOCOL section 4 step 4, which otherwise assigns that update to the receiving agent. Implementation committed as 2fe967f65d828c6fc0cc38c1ae550939122d6dc7 on feature/WF02-REQ023-20260816 (13 files, each staged by explicit name; no git add -A, no push, no PR).

issues.description: REQ-022's shipped design (req022-tenant-schema-provisioning.md sections 3.4 and 4) specifies tenant_scoped_migrations/0 as returning {version, module} tuples but does not account for priv/repo/migrations/*.exs never being compiled into the application (mix.exs elixirc_paths is [lib]). As shipped, the function would therefore have made replay_migrations/2 raise Ecto.MigrationError against any already-migrated database, and always under iex -S mix. Fixed in scope here under Unblock-Everything (body only; both shipped @specs byte-identical), and proven both ways in a fresh VM -- see result.summary's counterfactual. Reported so the req022 design document's section 3.4 can be amended to match the shipped code rather than being left silently divergent; the doc itself is untouched by this step.

Incidental, pre-existing, NOT fixed here (out of REQ-023's scope, touches 7 files this requirement does not own): .formatter.exs's inputs are [{mix,.formatter}.exs, {config,lib,test}/**/*.{ex,exs}] -- priv/repo/migrations/** is excluded, and the file declares no import_deps: [:ecto_sql]. Consequences: (a) migration files are never format-checked by the project's gate, and (b) running mix format --check-formatted explicitly against priv/repo/migrations/*.exs currently reports ALL 13 migrations as unformatted, because without import_deps: [:ecto_sql] the formatter has no locals_without_parens entry for add/2,3 and would rewrite every 'add :x, :y' to 'add(:x, :y)' and every 'create index(...)' to 'create(index(...))'. REQ-023's six new files deliberately match the shipped style of the seven existing ones, and the project's actual gate (bare mix format --check-formatted) exits 0. Recommend a separate requirement to add priv/repo/migrations/**/*.exs to inputs together with import_deps: [:ecto_sql], rather than an ad-hoc reformat.

Stale prose now that tenant_scoped_migrations/0 is no longer empty: test/specs/REQ-022.md:286 states in the present tense that tenant_scoped_migrations/0 'itself returns [] today (REQ-023 is the first real contributor per the design's section 3.4)', and test/support/req022_migration_fixture.ex:6 says the same. Both are TEST-DESIGNER-owned REQ-022 artefacts recording that run's own state, so neither was edited here. Forward note for Step 3: REVIEWER's REQ-022 Step 2d non-blocking suggestion of 'a lightweight guard test asserting each listed migration module no-ops under a nil prefix' is now actually writable, because tenant_scoped_migrations/0 has six entries to iterate over -- previously it had none, which is the only reason that test was written against the fixture module instead.

Design open question OQ-1, carried forward unresolved (raised at Step 1, restated so it is not lost between steps): event_retention_policies has no owning requirement anywhere in docs/requirements.yaml, yet REQ-026's archive logic is specified to consult it. Not created by this step, because doing so would expand REQ-023 past its acceptance-criteria-bounded six-table scope. Needs resolution -- extend REQ-026's scope or file it as its own requirement -- before REQ-026 starts.

Design open question OQ-2, carried forward unresolved: how large payloads survive archival is not settled by any source (R-Co offers no precedent because Store.archive() was retired there). event_payload_store's foreign key is therefore ON DELETE RESTRICT rather than R-Co's CASCADE, which makes the question fail loudly at REQ-026's first integration test instead of silently deleting archived tenant payloads. Confirmed present in the live catalog this step: 'event_payload_store_event_id_fkey: FOREIGN KEY (event_id, event_created_at) REFERENCES ...events(event_id, created_at) ON DELETE RESTRICT'.

Documentation discrepancy flagged per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL's own instruction to report conflicts rather than silently pick a side: HANDOFF_PROTOCOL section 4 step 4 tells the receiving agent to update the matching entry's status in handoffs/registry.json when completing a handoff, but this step's dispatch instruction states registry.json is ORCH-owned and must not be modified. The dispatch instruction was followed -- registry.json is untouched by this step and still needs ORCH to reflect this handoff's COMPLETED status.

Environment observation, not a code defect and not reproducible on retry: the first MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test invocation aborted before running any test with 'Could not start application letflow: Letflow.Application.start(:normal, []) returned an error: shutdown: failed to start child: {Bandit, ...} ** (EXIT) :eaddrinuse'. netstat showed nothing holding port 4000 immediately afterwards and the immediate retry passed 161/161. Bandit's listener port (4000) is not partitioned by MIX_TEST_PARTITION the way the database name is, so two concurrent worktree test runs on this host can collide on it. Recorded for ORCH in case concurrent-worktree runs become routine; no change made.
